scope: Film Programme homepage, desktop and mobile comparison board
prompt: Create a high-fidelity UX/UI DESIGN COMPARISON BOARD for Cinema Platform, a Ukrainian cinema website. This is an actual interface mockup, not a moodboard or poster, not code. Landscape board approximately 1800 by 1200. On the left show a large straight-on desktop homepage viewport with readable real interface regions (about 1240 by 930 at scale); on the right show a fully independent, correctly reflowed mobile homepage viewport (about 390 by 930 at scale), not a shrunken desktop. No perspective devices or computer props. Small neutral board label above each: Desktop, Mobile. BOTH views show the same Film Programme UX: visible navigation, film imagery and title, date context, clearly readable screening buttons directly beside/below that film, and the start of a second film entry below. Film-first editorial discovery, with integrated showtimes, never a uniform repeated card grid. Desktop and mobile opening viewport must include at least one usable-looking screening action without scrolling. Actual brand text "Cinema Platform". Ukrainian navigation "Фільми", "Розклад", "Квитки"; secondary "Увійти". Date "26 жовтня" and next-date choice "27 жовтня". Demo programme lead title "Дюна: Частина друга", secondary title "Памфір", third if space "Тіні забутих предків". Programme imagery: rich illustrative cinematic desert scene with a small cloaked figure, second film a photographic-looking rural Ukrainian forest scene. Imagery is illustrative not actual licensed movie stills. Lead screenings: "18:30 · Зал 1", "20:45 · Зал 2"; secondary "19:10 · Зал 1". Include small action "Усі сеанси". No prices, seat counts, availability guarantees, age ratings, screening formats, premiere dates, reviews, star ratings, recommendation claims, marketing statistics, or countdowns. Add a legible small footer outside both viewports: "Концепт · демонстраційна програма". Same content in both views. Exquisite polished typography and aligned meaningful controls; clear visual distinction between headings, metadata and actions. Keep text on solid contrasting surfaces, touch-sized mobile controls; text is not embedded illegibly over busy imagery. No decorative icon tiles, stock SaaS sections, glass panels, rounded card grid, gratuitous gradients or meaningless ornaments. Image must communicate actual homepage composition at finished visual fidelity. DIRECTION A — PROGRAMME PAPER. The digital equivalent of a thoughtfully typeset printed cinema programme, contemporary and tactile in restraint, not retro cosplay. Flat warm ivory #F2EBDD page, near-black olive ink #20251F, forest-green #3F513F functional selection/filled buttons, very restrained rust #A4492B small navigation indicator. Very subtle paper warmth, no distressed texture. Typography: large elegant editorial Cyrillic serif (PT Serif-like) for film titles, precise humanist sans for interface (PT Sans-like), tabular showtime numerals. Desktop: fine ruled masthead with text logo left and clear horizontal nav; below a compact editorial heading "Кіно на сьогодні" with date controls right. Main film is a sophisticated asymmetric magazine spread: generous large desert still occupying left 60%, title/synopsis and solid green screening actions in quiet ivory column at right; typographic title can span only its own column, never obscure art. A thin-rule caption "01" connects image and title. Secondary film begins as a compact horizontal entry with smaller image on right and title/time on left, proving varied scale rather than cards. Wide meaningful margins and fine horizontal separators, imagery warm and full-color. Mobile: compact wordmark and text "Квитки" + menu; visible date selector, film title, widescreen image with shorter height, then full-width readable showtime buttons on ivory; second film entry begins visibly below. Keep main film's date and time visible within mobile viewport. The page feels like a real cinema publication with practical booking, not an art gallery without controls.
contentProvenance: Illustrative programme and generated film-like imagery; not retrieved catalogue content, actual screenings, or licensed film stills.
